members.summary: Decides, on a schedule, how many singular triplets each AdaLoRA layer keeps.
members.extended:
Reference: Zhang et al., 2023 (AdaLoRA).  The allocator reads the
sensitivity of the adapter's tensors after every backward pass
(`update_ipt`), and on the steps the budget schedule marks, masks
the least important triplets of the whole model down to the budget
(`mask_to_budget`).  `update_and_allocate` is the one call a
training step makes, and `AdaLoraModel.update_and_allocate` makes it for
the model.

The budget starts at the model's total number of triplets, stays there
for `tinit` steps, falls on a cubic schedule to `target_r` triplets
per layer at step `total_step - tfinal` and stays there.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model AdaLoRA was applied to.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: The adapter's config: the schedule and the moving-average weights.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: The adapter that trains.

raises.description: `adapter_name` is not held by any AdaLoRA layer of `model`.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.adalora import AdaLoraConfig, AdaLoraModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(6, 6), nn.Linear(6, 2))
>>> config = AdaLoraConfig(init_r=4, target_r=2, total_step=20, tfinal=5, target_modules=["0", "1"])
>>> allocator = AdaLoraModel(net, config, "default").rankallocator
>>> tuple(allocator.budget_schedule(0)), tuple(allocator.budget_schedule(19))
((8, False), (4, True))

methods.name: to_dict
methods.summary: Return the config as the JSON-ready dict `adapter_config.json` holds.
methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.  A field the reference's config of this method lacks
(`IA3Config.layers_to_transform`) is written only when it is set,
so a file that does not use it is one the reference reads too.

returns.description: One entry per field, keyed by the reference's field names.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> d = LoraConfig(target_modules=["v", "q"], task_type="CAUSAL_LM").to_dict()
>>> d["target_modules"], d["task_type"], d["peft_type"]
(['q', 'v'], 'CAUSAL_LM', 'LORA')

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"loftq_config": {}`, `"megatron_config": null`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is dropped.  Called on
`PeftConfig`, the dict's `peft_type` picks the class.

parameters.name: config_dict
parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class the dict's method names.

raises.description:
The dict describes another adapter type, or turns on a feature
v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})

methods.name: from_peft_type
methods.summary: Build a config from its fields given as keyword arguments, the class chosen by `peft_type`.
methods.extended:
The reference's way to turn the keys of a config file into a config: the
`peft_type` argument names the method and so the class, whichever class this is
called on.  Without one, the calling class is built.  The fields are read as
`from_dict` reads them, so a key this library has no field for is accepted
at a value that turns its feature off (dropped, with a warning when the key is
unknown), where the reference drops it at any value.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description: The config's fields, by name; `peft_type` is a `PeftType` or its string.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class `peft_type` names.

raises.description: `peft_type` names no method of this library.
No `peft_type` is given and this is `PeftConfig` itself, which builds no config of its own.
A key turns on a feature this library does not implement.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> config = PeftConfig.from_peft_type(peft_type="LORA", r=4, target_modules=["q"])
>>> type(config).__name__, config.r
('LoraConfig', 4)
>>> LoraConfig.from_peft_type(r=2, target_modules=["q"]).r
2

members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with AdaLoRA.
members.extended:
AdaLoRA (Zhang et al., 2023, [arXiv:2303.10512](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10512)) writes the update of a
targeted `nn.Linear` (or `nn.Conv2d`) as a truncated SVD,

$$
\qquad P \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times r},\;
\lambda \in \mathbb{R}^{r},\;
Q \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{in}},
$$

with $P, Q$ kept near-orthogonal by a penalty on the loss, and
learns how many of the $r$ singular triplets each layer deserves:
the importance of each triplet is tracked during training and the least
important are masked away on a schedule until the model holds
`target_r` triplets per layer on average
(`lucid.peft.tuners.adalora.AdaLoraModel.update_and_allocate`).

Training has three phases, set by `tinit`, `tfinal` and `total_step`:
the first `tinit` steps train every triplet; then the budget falls on a
cubic schedule until step `total_step - tfinal`, where it reaches
`target_r` per layer; the last `tfinal` steps fine-tune what is left.
With `tinit = 10`, `tfinal = 20` and `total_step = 100`, 10 steps
warm up, 70 steps shrink the budget and 20 steps fine-tune.

Field names, their order, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the
reference adapter library's.  Its `LoraConfig` fields that AdaLoRA does
not use (`use_rslora`, `use_dora`, `lora_bias`, `alpha_pattern` …)
and the ones this package lacks (`eva_config`, `use_qalora` …) are
fields too, at the reference's defaults; any other value raises
`NotImplementedError` naming the field.

triplet's sensitivity; in `(0, 1)`.

parameters.name: beta2

parameters.name: orth_reg_weight

parameters.name: total_step

`tinit + tfinal`.

raises.description: A field holds a value of the wrong type.

A field is out of range, `total_step` is missing, or the schedule
leaves no room for the budget to fall (`tinit >= total_step - tfinal`).
`bias` is not `"none"`.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.adalora import AdaLoraConfig
>>> config = AdaLoraConfig(init_r=12, target_r=4, total_step=100, target_modules=["q", "v"])
>>> sorted(config.target_modules), config.peft_type
(['q', 'v'], <PeftType.ADALORA: 'ADALORA'>)
>>> AdaLoraConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True

methods.summary: Create adapter `adapter_name` with `r` singular triplets.
methods.extended:
The tensors live on the base weight's device, in its dtype — float32
for a half-precision base.  With `init_lora_weights` the singular
values start at zero, so the adapted layer starts as the base.  A
layer that holds an adapter already keeps applying the adapters it
applied: the new one is inactive until `set_adapter` names it.

methods.name: merge
methods.signature: merge(safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Fold the update into the base weights, in place.
methods.extended:
The weights keep their identity — they are written, not replaced —
so whatever holds them (an optimizer, a tied embedding) sees the
merged values.  That is also why a weight shared with another
module must not be merged into; the tuner's `merge_adapter` and
`merge_and_unload` refuse it, as this layer alone cannot see the
rest of the model.

Merging some of the active adapters leaves the rest applying: the layer's
forward pass runs the folded weights and then the active adapters that are
not folded, so it computes what it did unmerged.  The reference runs a
merged layer's base alone, which drops the others — a deliberate departure
(LCD-971).  A method whose adapters would not compute the same function
that way (rotations that must apply in order, DoRA reading the weight)
refuses the split in the tuner's `merge_adapter`, before it writes
anything; this method, called on a layer directly, does not check it.
Merging an adapter that is not active adds it: the layer then runs the weights
with it folded in and the active adapters it has not folded (the base with that
adapter alone, in the reference).

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description:
Check the merged weights for NaN / inf first and leave the base

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Adapters to merge; the active ones this layer holds by default.

raises.description:
An adapter name this layer does not hold, or `safe_merge`

The adapter is disabled, or the layer's own rules refuse the merge
(`lora_bias` on a base with no bias).
This layer's update cannot be written into its base weights.

methods.name: unmerge
methods.summary: Take every merged update back out of the base weights, in place.
methods.extended:
The result equals the original weights up to the rounding of the
round trip.

members.summary: Adapter bookkeeping shared by the AdaLoRA layers.
members.extended:
Holds the wrapped module as `base_layer` — the very module, so its
parameters stay the same `Parameter` objects — and, per adapter name,
the three tensors in `lora_A` / `lora_B` / `lora_E` and the
frozen `ranknum` (`ParameterDict`s, so a state dict reads
`....lora_E.default` and an adapter file `....lora_E`).  The forward
pass adds the update of every active adapter this layer holds.

members.signature: SVDLinear(base_layer: nn.Module, adapter_name: str, config: AdaLoraConfig, r: int = 0, lora_alpha: float = 1)
members.summary: An `nn.Linear` with an SVD-parameterised update: $y = W x + b + \tfrac{\alpha}{\mathrm{ranknum}}\,P\,\mathrm{diag}(\lambda)\,Q\,\mathrm{drop}(x)$.
members.extended:
The update is applied as three small products, never as an `(out, in)`
matrix, so a layer pruned to a few triplets costs a few triplets.  Stackable: the triplets'
update is added to the output of whichever layer it stands on.

>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.adalora import AdaLoraConfig
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.adalora import SVDLinear
>>> base = nn.Linear(8, 4)
>>> layer = SVDLinear(base, "default", AdaLoraConfig(total_step=10), r=3, lora_alpha=6)
>>> tuple(layer.lora_A["default"].shape), tuple(layer.lora_E["default"].shape)
((3, 8), (3, 1))
>>> x = lucid.randn(2, 8)
>>> bool((layer(x) == base(x)).all().item())   # the singular values start at zero

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Call the model, adding the orthogonality penalty to its loss.
methods.extended:
When the output carries a `loss` and an adapter trains, `orth_reg_weight` times the
penalty that keeps $P$ and $Q$ near-orthogonal is added to it; otherwise the
output is returned as it is.

methods.name: update_and_allocate
methods.summary: Record the importance of every triplet and, on schedule, mask the least important ones.
methods.extended:
Call it every training step, after `loss.backward()` and before the
gradients are cleared.  `tinit`, `tfinal` and `deltaT` are
handled here: until `total_step - tfinal` the allocator masks down to
the falling budget; at that step it masks to `target_r` per layer,
stores the rank pattern in the config and forgets the importances;
afterwards it keeps the dropped triplets at zero.

adapter is for inference.

methods.name: add_adapter
methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter starts frozen and inactive: the forward pass keeps
applying the adapters it applied, and every parameter keeps the
`requires_grad` it had.  `set_adapter` switches to it.  A
module an earlier adapter already wraps takes the new one beside
it; any other target is wrapped.  The model is left as it was if
the adapter cannot be added.

Layers that hold merged adapters stay merged, bit for bit, and the
adapter starts from the weights as they were before the merge, as it
would on the unmerged model.  An initialisation that writes the base
weights (PiSSA, OLoRA, LoRA-GA) cannot be applied where adapters are
merged: `unmerge_adapter` first.

initialisation writes the base weights of a layer that holds

`config` is not an adapter config.

Every other adapter is frozen; the activated ones train unless
`inference_mode`.  A merged layer is unmerged first.  Layers that
hold none of the named adapters run their base alone.  The
parameters `bias` makes trainable follow the adapter that asked
for them.

methods.name: delete_adapter
methods.summary: Remove an adapter: its parameters, its config, its `modules_to_save` copies.
methods.extended:
If it was active, the adapters still active stay so; when none
remain the first of the others (by name) takes over, with a
warning, and trains.  Deleting the last adapter leaves the layers
in the model, applying nothing; `unload()` removes them.

raises.description: The adapter does not exist, or it is merged — unmerge first.

methods.name: merge_adapter
methods.signature: merge_adapter(adapter_names: list[str] | None = None, safe_merge: bool = False)
methods.summary: Fold adapter updates into their base weights, keeping the adapter layers.
methods.extended:
A merged model runs at the base model's cost; `unmerge_adapter`
takes the updates out again.  Every refusal is made before any
weight is written: nothing is merged if a layer's base weight is
shared with another module (a tied LM head — merging would change
that module too) or if the adapter is disabled.

Merging some of the active adapters leaves the others applying: a merged
layer runs its folded weights and then the active adapters it has not
folded, so the model computes what it did unmerged.  The reference runs a
merged layer's base alone, which drops the others; Lucid departs from that
on purpose (LCD-971).  Merging an adapter that is not active adds it: the
layers then run the weights with it folded in and the active adapters they
have not folded (the base with that adapter alone, in the reference).  A
method whose adapters do not compute the same function once split refuses
it: those that apply in order (OFT, BOFT, HRA, RoAd's `road_2` and
`road_4`, MiSS / Bone's `bat`) take only the first of the active
adapters, in their order; a LoRA layer refuses to fold some adapters while
a DoRA one stays unmerged; LN tuning, which runs one adapter's copy at a
time, refuses to fold an active adapter while another is active.

A name is not one of the model's adapters, `safe_merge` found a
non-finite merged weight, or a layer's method cannot go on applying
the active adapters that stay unmerged.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False)
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4)), config)
>>> peft.add_adapter("two", config)
>>> peft.base_model.set_adapter(["default", "two"])
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> both = peft(x)
>>> peft.base_model.merge_adapter(adapter_names=["default"])
>>> peft.base_model.model[0].merged_adapters
['default']
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(peft(x), both, atol=1e-5))   # "two" still applies
True

methods.summary: Merge the adapters into the base weights and return the plain model.

Each adapter layer is replaced by its merged base module — the base
model's own module, holding its own `Parameter` objects — and each
`modules_to_save` entry by the active adapter's trained copy (the
original when that adapter has none).  Adapters not merged are
dropped with their layers.  Every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

members.summary: A model with AdaLoRA layers put into it, the rank allocation and the tools to take them out.
members.extended:
Construction replaces each module `config` selects with an AdaLoRA layer
around it — `lucid.peft.tuners.adalora.SVDLinear` or `SVDConv2d`,
by the module's type — and freezes every other parameter.  The model is
changed in place and kept as `model`; a public name this wrapper lacks is
read from it.  `config` itself is not changed: `peft_config` holds a
copy with the default `target_modules` spelled out.

**Training.**  Call `update_and_allocate` once per step, after
`loss.backward()` and before the gradients are cleared; it records how
much each singular triplet matters and, on the schedule `tinit` /
`tfinal` / `deltaT` / `total_step` define, masks the least important
ones until `target_r` per layer remain.  The forward pass adds the
orthogonality penalty `orth_reg_weight * mean(||Q Q^T - I||, ||P^T P - I||)`
to the output's `loss` when it has one, so the model has to be called
through this wrapper (or a `PeftModel`) to be penalised.

**One trainable adapter.**  Several adapters may be held, but only one may
train: give every other config `inference_mode=True`.  The rank allocator
follows the one that trains.

**In a mixed model** (`mixed=True`) AdaLoRA is for inference: `MixedModel` neither
runs the rank allocator nor adds the orthogonality penalty, which are this class's.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to adapt.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in every `lora_*` table.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
`low_cpu_mem_usage` and `state_dict` of `lucid.peft.LoraModel`, which the
reference's AdaLoRA tuner forwards.  Neither is implemented: a value other than the
default raises `NotImplementedError`, and any other key `TypeError`.

raises.description:
No module matches `target_modules`, a match is a module type with no
AdaLoRA layer, `modules_to_save` matches nothing, or a second
trainable adapter is asked for.

The model already holds adapter layers (wrap it once; add adapters
with `add_adapter`).

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.adalora import AdaLoraConfig, AdaLoraModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(8, 2))
>>> config = AdaLoraConfig(init_r=4, target_r=2, total_step=10, target_modules=["0"])
>>> ada = AdaLoraModel(net, config, "default")
>>> ada.targeted_module_names, net[0].r["default"]
(['0'], 4)
>>> ada(lucid.randn(3, 8)).sum().backward()
>>> ada.update_and_allocate(1)
>>> ada.unload() is net, type(net[0]) is nn.Linear
(True, True)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.adalora` — AdaLoRA: LoRA whose rank per layer is allocated while it trains.
extended:
AdaLoRA (Zhang et al., 2023, [arXiv:2303.10512](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10512)) writes the update of a layer as a truncated SVD,
$\Delta W = \frac{\alpha}{\mathrm{ranknum}}\,P\,\mathrm{diag}(\lambda)\,Q$, with $P$ and
$Q$ kept near-orthogonal by a penalty on the loss.  It tracks how much each singular triplet
matters during training and masks the least important ones on a schedule, so a fixed parameter
budget goes to the layers that need it.  Pick it over LoRA when you know the budget but not which
layers deserve the rank; call `AdaLoraModel.update_and_allocate` after each optimizer step.

Where the reference library keeps them, so `isinstance(m, AdaLoraLayer)` and `from
lucid.peft.tuners.adalora import AdaLoraConfig, SVDLinear` read as they do there.  One layer type
per module the method adapts: `SVDLinear` and `SVDConv2d`; `RankAllocator` is the budget
schedule.  `AdaLoraConfig` and `AdaLoraModel` are here and exported from `lucid.peft`.
Importing the package registers the method (its config under `PeftType.ADALORA`, its tuner and
layers), which is what makes `get_peft_model` and `PeftModel.from_pretrained` know it.
citation: Zhang, Qingru, et al. "Adaptive Budget Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning." [arXiv:2303.10512](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10512), 2023.
theory:
AdaLoRA (Zhang et al., 2023, [arXiv:2303.10512](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10512)) writes the update of a
targeted `nn.Linear` (or `nn.Conv2d`) as a truncated SVD,

$$
\qquad P \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times r},\;
\lambda \in \mathbb{R}^{r},\;
Q \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{in}},
$$
